August, 2024
 The Hon'Ble Smt.Justice M.G.Priyadarsini
 M.A.C.M.A.No.168 of 2019

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1. Dissatisfied with the compensation awarded by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (District Judge), Nizamabad, in M.V.O.P.No.422 of 2016, dated 03.05.2018, the claim petitioner therein filed the present Appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (District Judge), Nizamabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties hereinafter be referred as they were arrayed before the Tribunal.

3. The facts of the case in brief are that the claim petitioner filed a petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- against the respondents on account of the injuries sustained by him in a Motor vehicle accident that occurred on 18.03.2016.

It is stated by the claim petitioner that on 18.03.2016 at about 2.30 P.M. when the petitioner and his son were going on Activa Bearing No.TS-16EF- 1588 from Dichpally Village to Kondapur Village and when reached near Dichpally Arch, Bibipur Thanda Sivar on NH-44 Road, in the meantime, the driver of one Car bearing No.KL02Y100 lost control over the Car and drove the car in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the petitioner and his son.
As a result, the petitioner and his Son fell down from the said Activa vehicle and sustained fractures and multiple injuries all over the body.

The petitioner sustained fracture of both bones of right leg and fracture of right MGP,J shoulder,
multiple and grievous injuries on face, both hands and legs and all over the body.

Immediately, he was shifted in '108' Ambulance to Government Hospital where he was given First Aid and referred to higher centre for expert treatment and he was shifted to RR Life Line Hospital, Nizamabad and underwent treatment as inpatient from 18.03.2016 to 23.03.2016 and underwent operation on 19.03.2016 and steel rods were implanted.
Police of Dichpally Police Station registered a case in Crime No.53 of 2016 under Section 337 IPC.
It is further contended that the petitioner was aged 40 years and was a Toddy Tapper-cum- Agriculturist and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained by him, he lost his income and also incurred Rs.3,00,000/- towards his treatment and became permanently disabled and became dependant on others.

Hence, filed claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- from the respondent Nos.1 & 2.
4.

Respondent No.1, who is the owner of the Car bearing No.KL02Y100, filed his counter denying the averments of the claim petition and contended that he is having valid and subsisting driving license as on the date of accident and contended that as the vehicle was insured with respondent No.2, the Insurance Company is only liable to pay the compensation and prayed to dismiss the claim against him.

sentences.text: Respondent No.2/Insurance Company filed its counter denying the averments made in the claim petition and contended that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Activa bearing No.TS-16EF-1588 and contended that the owner and Insurance Company of Activa are necessary parties to the case and the alleged accident occurred due to the contributory negligence of the drivers of both the vehicles and that the claim of compensation is excess and exorbitant and hence, prayed to dismiss the claim against it.

6. Based on the above pleadings, the learned Tribunal had framed the following issues:-
(i) Whether the petitioner received injuries in the motor accident due to rash and negligent driving of the car bearing No.KL02Y100 by its driver?
(ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what extent and from whom?

(iii) To what relief?
7.
Before the Tribunal, the claim petitioner was examined himself as PW1, got examined PW2 and got marked Exs.A1 to A13 on his behalf.
On behalf of the respondents, no oral evidence was adduced, however, Ex.B1-Copy of insurance policy was marked through consent.
MGP,J 8.

After considering the evidence and documents filed by both sides, the learned Tribunal had awarded an amount of Rs.1,23,000/- as compensation along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till date of realization.
9. Not satisfied with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claim petitioner preferred the present Appeal seeking enhancement of the same.

10. Heard the submission of the learned counsel for the appellant as well as the learned Standing Counsel for the respondent No.2/ Insurance Company.
11.

The main contention of the learned counsel for appellant is that though the claim petitioner has proved his case by adducing cogent and convincing evidence and also got examined PW2, who is the Doctor who treated him and also filed all the relevant documents, however, the learned Tribunal,
without considering the same, had awarded meagre amount towards compensation and hence prayed to allow the Appeal by enhancing the compensation.
12.

Per contra, learned Standing Counsel for the respondent No.2/Insurance Company argued that the learned Tribunal, after considering all the aspects, had awarded reasonable compensation and interference of this Court is unwarranted.

sentences.text: Now the point that emerges for determination is, MGP,J
Whether the order passed by the learned Tribunal suffers from any irregularity?
POINT:-
14. This Court has perused the entire evidence and documents filed by both sides.
The claim petitioner, who examined himself as PW1, had reiterated the contents of the claim petition and deposed about the manner of accident and also the injuries sustained by him .
In order to prove the injuries and the treatment undergone by him, he got examined PW2 -Dr.K.Ramesh,Orthopaedic Surgeon.

15. PW2, who is an Orthopaedic Surgeon, RR Lifeline Hospital, deposed that on 18.03.2016, he examined the petitioner and found two injuries which are, (i) Swelling and deformity on right leg corresponding X-ray shows fracture to both bones right leg and (ii) Swelling and deformity on right shoulder corresponding X-ray shows acromeo cavity joint.

The said two injuries are grievous in nature and the petitioner was treated conservatively for the 2nd injury and the 1st injury is managed by closed reduction and internal fixation with intern locking nail right tibia.
Ex.X1- Case Sheet was got marked through him.
16. Though PWs 1 & 2 were cross-examined at length, nothing worthy was elicited from them to disbelieve their evidence.
In fact, the cross-examination of PW2 is nothing but mere suggestions.
Therefore, it is clear that there is no dispute regarding the manner of accident, injuries sustained by the claim petitioner in the road MGP,J traffic accident.
Apart from oral evidence, the petitioner had also relied upon documentary evidence under Exs.A1 to A13.

Ex.A1- FIR discloses that Police of Ditchpally Police Station registered a case in Crime No.53 of 2006 under Section 337, took up investigation and laid charge sheet under Ex.A2 against the driver of the Car bearing No.KL-02Y-100.
Ex. A3
- Injury certificate discloses the injuries sustained by the claim petitioner in the road traffic accident.
Ex . A4
is the Crime details form.
Ex . A5
is the Discharge Summary.
Ex . A6
is the Hospital Bill.
Ex . A7
are the cash bills.
Ex . A8
are the prescriptions.
Ex . A9
is the Investigation report.
Ex . A10
are the Medical bills.
Ex . A11
are the X-ray films (5 in number).
Ex . A12
is the Driving license.
Ex . A13
= Ex .
B1- Insurance policy indicates that the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Exs . A3, A5, A6, A7, A8, A10 & A11 disclose the treatment undergone by the claim petitioner.
Therefore, it is clear that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the crime vehicle.
This Court do not find any reason to interfere with the finding of the learned Tribunal.

17. Now, coming to the aspect of compensation, the learned Tribunal had awarded an amount of Rs.40,000/- towards pain and suffering, an amount of Rs.45,000/- towards medical expenses; an amount of Rs.18,000/- towards loss of earnings for a period of three months; an amount of Rs.20,000/- towards transportation and extra nourishment.

This Court, by considering the nature of MGP,J injuries sustained by the petitioner, is of the considerable opinion to award an amount of Rs.25,000/- each for two grievous injuries and an amount of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical treatment.

Due to the injuries sustained by the petitioner, he is deprived of simple pleasures and Kannapuram Saya Goud vs Jhon George And Another on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119858996/
3 amenities of life for which, he is put to severe inconvenience, hardship, discomfort, disappointment,
frustration and mental stress in life and hence awarded a sum of Rs.7,000/- towards the same.

In the result, the Appeal filed by the claimant is partly- allowed by enhancing the compensation awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.1,23,000/- to Rs.2,00,000/-.

The enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization payable by the respondent Nos.1 & 2 jointly and severally within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and upon such payment made, the appellant/claimant is entitled to withdraw the same without furnishing any security.
There shall be no order as to costs.
